scope: Selective primary-source review of reference correction, residual control, contact adaptation and planning-plus-RL. Related methods are distinguished from direct trajectory trackers. Repository availability was checked; packages were not installed or reproduced.

papers.title: Real-Robot Deep Reinforcement Learning: Improving Trajectory Tracking of Flexible-Joint Manipulator with Reference Correction
papers.method: An outer-loop policy modifies joint references using tracking error, recent history and upcoming reference points.
papers.evidence: Physical Baxter, SAC training and unseen-payload evaluation. Corrections run at 20 Hz, filtered at 4 Hz.
papers.fit: Directly matches trajectory correction for robot dynamics errors. It assumes a valid reference; incorrect hinge geometry requires a different objective.
papers.human_data: Random reference trajectories; no manipulation demonstration required.
papers.code_note: Author paper/video verified; repository not verified.

papers.title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Robot Control
papers.method: Combine an existing feedback controller with a learned additive residual. The controller supplies useful nominal behavior; learning compensates for interactions that are difficult to model.
papers.evidence: Physical block assembly with friction, contacts and unstable objects.
papers.fit: A direct precedent for retaining a model-based controller while learning local corrections. Our planner would supply the nominal motion; adding reference-window conditioning would be our adaptation.
papers.human_data: Uses an engineered base controller rather than requiring a human demonstration.
papers.code_note: Project and paper verified; implementation repository not verified in this review.

papers.title: Residual Policy Learning
papers.method: Learn corrections around supplied policies, including hand-designed controllers and model predictive control.
papers.evidence: Six simulated MuJoCo tasks covering partial observation, noise, model misspecification and miscalibration.
papers.fit: Useful for studying which errors a residual can compensate for while keeping the nominal planner fixed. Its results do not establish transfer to our particular drawer or microwave.
papers.human_data: An initial policy is required; human demonstration is not intrinsic to the formulation.
papers.code_note: Public author repository verified; not installed or reproduced.

papers.title: Residual Learning from Demonstration: Adapting DMPs for Contact-rich Manipulation
papers.method: A demonstration-derived dynamic movement primitive supplies nominal motion; RL learns residual corrections in the full end-effector pose space.
papers.evidence: Simulated and physical peg, gear and plug insertion; few-shot adaptation to changed geometry and friction.
papers.fit: Very close to the teacher-trajectory version of the user's idea. Replacing the demonstrated primitive with our planned trajectory is a proposed adaptation, not a reported result of this paper.
papers.human_data: Uses demonstrations. Relevant to future one-shot work, not the current demonstration-free setup.
papers.code_note: Author project and videos verified; implementation repository not verified in this review.

papers.title: Variable Impedance Control in End-Effector Space: An Action Space for Reinforcement Learning in Contact-Rich Tasks
papers.method: RL commands end-effector motion and impedance, adjusting contact compliance.
papers.evidence: Path, door and wiping studies; physical Panda wiping. Policy: 20 Hz; torque controller: 500 Hz.
papers.fit: Relevant to uncertain contact paths. An action-space study, not an external-trajectory tracker; real door-opening performance is not claimed here.
papers.human_data: RL training; no one-shot demonstration requirement.
papers.code_note: Public robosuite research branch verified; dependency adaptation required.

papers.title: Learning Force Control for Contact-rich Manipulation Tasks with Rigid Position-controlled Robots
papers.method: Combines RL with parallel position/force control or admittance control for robots exposing a position-control interface.
papers.evidence: Simulation and real UR3e experiments compare the two force-control action spaces.
papers.fit: Shows that contact-aware learning need not replace every low-level motor controller. We would need a legitimate force estimate or sensor interface; native simulator contact identities must remain evaluation-only.
papers.human_data: Learned through interaction; a force-control structure is engineered.
papers.code_note: Paper and its linked demonstration video verified; implementation repository not verified in this review.

papers.title: Open Sesame! Adaptive Force/Velocity Control for Opening Unknown Doors
papers.method: An adaptive force/velocity controller estimates the constrained radial direction while regulating contact force and tangential motion during door opening.
papers.evidence: Simulation and physical robot experiments with initially unknown door geometry.
papers.fit: A direct non-RL baseline for hinge-estimation error: adapt to the physical constraint instead of forcing a guessed circular path. It assumes an established contact/grasp and force/torque feedback, so it does not solve selecting the wrong handle.
papers.human_data: No demonstration or RL training; adaptive control assumptions still apply.
papers.code_note: Primary accepted-manuscript text retrieved through search; direct PDF fetch was intermittently unavailable. No repository verified.

papers.title: FORGE: Force-Guided Exploration for Robust Contact-Rich Manipulation under Uncertainty
papers.method: Force-conditioned RL combines dynamics randomization, a maximum allowable force input and learned task-success prediction for uncertain assembly.
papers.evidence: Physical assembly demonstrations include snap-fit and planetary-gear tasks under pose uncertainty.
papers.fit: Relevant to reducing force while completing a contact task, rather than treating pose-tracking accuracy as the only objective. It is not presented as a general external-trajectory follower.
papers.human_data: Simulation-trained RL; its demonstrated training setup must be accounted for in comparisons.
papers.code_note: Official project and publication verified; implementation repository not verified in this review.

papers.title: IndustReal: Transferring Contact-Rich Assembly Tasks from Simulation to Reality
papers.method: Simulation RL for assembly is paired with a policy-level action integrator (PLAI) that accumulates policy increments in the desired state. A leaky variant limits excessive accumulation.
papers.evidence: Real Panda assembly deployment, with public simulation, hardware and deployment tools.
papers.fit: Shows why translating policy increments into controller references affects sim-to-real performance. PLAI is a deployment rule, not itself a learned residual; observations still feed the policy. Our measured-hand reset is a different rule and needs its own comparison.
papers.human_data: RL in simulation; deployment calibration and task infrastructure are still required.
papers.code_note: IndustRealLib deployment repository verified. Official project also links Isaac Gym/Isaac Lab simulation code and IndustRealKit hardware.

papers.title: TRANSIC: Sim-to-Real Policy Transfer by Learning from Online Correction
papers.method: A base policy is trained in simulation. Human teleoperation corrections during real deployment train a gated residual policy, which is subsequently combined with the base policy.
papers.evidence: Physical FurnitureBench assembly, including tasks with coexisting perception, dynamics and controller gaps.
papers.fit: An established way to repair simulated skills with real corrections. Online correction here includes human intervention and later policy learning; it is not automatic zero-demo adaptation during the first deployment.
papers.human_data: Human corrective demonstrations are essential to the transfer procedure.
papers.code_note: Author project provides algorithm code, simulator code, models and data links. No installation or reproduction performed.

papers.title: Motion Planner Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Robot Manipulation in Obstructed Environments
papers.method: A policy uses direct actions for small motions and invokes motion planning for larger moves, combining local interaction with longer collision-aware travel.
papers.evidence: Simulated Sawyer manipulation with obstructions, including pushing, lifting and assembly.
papers.fit: Strong precedent for combining motion planning and RL. Its switching construction differs from continuously correcting one fixed master trajectory.
papers.human_data: RL with planner access; human demonstration is not the key dependency.
papers.code_note: Public author repository verified. Its older Python/MuJoCo stack would need a port or isolated environment.

papers.title: Plan-Seq-Learn: Language Model Guided RL for Solving Long Horizon Robotics Tasks
papers.method: Language-model task decomposition specifies regions and stage conditions; motion planning connects them and RL learns local control.
papers.evidence: More than 25 long-horizon simulation tasks spanning four benchmarks in the paper.
papers.fit: A particularly important prior for any VLM/LLM plus motion planner plus learned control claim. It is broader than trajectory residual learning and requires control-policy training; its results are not a zero-training LIBERO benchmark for our setup.
papers.human_data: Learns control from interaction rather than assuming a fixed predefined skill library.
papers.code_note: Public author repository verified; not installed or reproduced.

papers.title: Guided Policy Search
papers.method: Trajectory optimization guides policy learning, using optimized local behavior to train a feedback policy.
papers.evidence: The original paper evaluates simulated control and locomotion tasks.
papers.fit: Relevant when a planner acts as a training teacher. This does not necessarily leave an explicit master trajectory supplied to the policy at deployment; that distinction matters for our proposed architecture.
papers.human_data: Optimized trajectories rather than human demonstrations guide the original method.
papers.code_note: Primary proceedings paper verified; no implementation selected.

papers.title: DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills
papers.method: Reference-motion imitation and task objectives train a feedback policy that executes skills under physics and responds to perturbations.
papers.evidence: Simulated articulated characters performing dynamic skills from motion examples.
papers.fit: A clear precedent for reference trajectories producing reactive execution, but character animation is not evidence of accurate Panda handle manipulation.
papers.code_note: Author project provides code links; no implementation installed.

papers.title: RMA: Rapid Motor Adaptation for Legged Robots
papers.method: A simulation-trained adaptation module infers changing environment/dynamics information from recent experience and conditions a base policy.
papers.evidence: Real legged locomotion under varied terrain and payload without deployment-time fine-tuning.
papers.fit: Suggests conditioning contact execution on recent interaction history. It is neither a manipulator trajectory tracker nor proof that an unobserved hinge is identifiable from arbitrary contact.
papers.human_data: Simulation training; no human motion demonstration is essential to this approach.
papers.code_note: Primary proceedings and author project verified; no implementation selected.

papers.title: Bettering operation of Robots by learning
papers.method: Iterative learning control improves a repeated operation by updating the next trial's input using the previous trial's tracking error.
papers.evidence: Foundational robot learning-control formulation for repeated motions.
papers.fit: Relevant to replaying the same planned task, but trial-to-trial improvement is different from reacting to an unexpected contact within a single first attempt. It can coexist with feedback control.
papers.human_data: Repeated execution experience is required, not necessarily human demonstration.
papers.code_note: Primary publisher source verified; not a current software package.
